```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

H1: Women will score higher on intensity of love compared to men.

H2: Overall romantic love will positively correlate with relationship duration.

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("PSY221A_Negrette/Data/Raw/data_doctored.csv")
dim(raw)
head(raw)


#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows






data <- raw[, c("ResponseId","Sex","Love_how_much_1","Relationship_length",
                "Love_1","Love_2","Love_3","Love_4","Love_5","Love_6","Love_7","Love_8","Love_9","Love_10","Love_11","Love_12","Love_13","Love_14","Love_15")]






```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))
#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm = T)
#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))
#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingID,]

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```


## 3. Recode gender

```{r sex_at_birth}

table(data$Sex,useNA="ifany")
#0=Men; 1=Women; 2=Non-binary; 3=Prefer not to say.

data$Sex <- factor(data$Sex,
                   levels = c(0,1,2,3),
                   labels = c("Men","Women","Non-binary","Prefer not to say"))



```


## 4. Validate Love Intensity

```{r preference_vars}

table(data$Love_how_much_1,useNA ="ifany")

# Confirm scores are within the intended 0–100 range
sum(h1Data$Love_how_much_1 < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(h1Data$Love_how_much_1 > 100, na.rm = TRUE)






#make h1Data with ID, Sex, and love intensity


h1Data <- data[, c("ResponseId", "Sex", "Love_how_much_1")]

h1Data <- h1Data[
  !is.na(h1Data$Sex) &
  !is.na(h1Data$Love_how_much_1),
]

str(h1Data)
summary(h1Data)
```


## 5. Overall romantic love
```{r Overall romantic love}
#group all fifteen love variables

all_love <- c("Love_1","Love_2","Love_3","Love_4","Love_5","Love_6","Love_7","Love_8","Love_9","Love_10","Love_11","Love_12","Love_13","Love_14","Love_15")
love_items <- data[, all_love]
str(love_items)
summary(love_items)

lapply(love_items, function(x) table(x, useNA = "ifany"))
#range 
sapply(love_items, function(x)
  sum(x < 1 | x > 5, na.rm = TRUE)
)

colSums(is.na(love_items))


#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing

data$all_love_score <- ifelse(
  answered_items >= 12,
  rowSums(data[, all_love], na.rm = TRUE),
  NA
)


#pplthat did not complete atleast 12 of 15
answered_items <- rowSums(!is.na(data[, all_love]))

data$all_love_score <- ifelse(
  answered_items >= 12,
  rowSums(data[, all_love], na.rm = TRUE),
  NA
)
#check the score
summary(data$all_love_score)


```

## 6. Calculate relationship duration

```{r relationship duration}
table(data$Relationship_length,useNA ="ifany")

# Confirm scores are within the intended 0–100 range
sum(data$Relationship_length < 1, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(data$Relationship_length > 80, na.rm = TRUE)




#check the score
summary(data$Relationship_length)


#make h2Data with ID, relationship duration, and love intensity
#do not apply the H1 preference filter to this hypothesis



h2Data <- data[, c("ResponseId", "Relationship_length", "all_love_score")]



h2Data <- h2Data[
  !is.na(h2Data$Relationship_length) &
  !is.na(h2Data$all_love_score),
]
summary(h2Data)

```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$Sex,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$Love_how_much_1)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$all_love_score)
range(h2Data$Relationship_length)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Reported Gender: original codes #0=Men; 1=Women; 2=Non-binary; 3=Prefer not to say; now stored as a factor",
  "Single item continous variable measuring love intesnity ; 0-100 points from ; zero is valid"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Relationship length: Asks how long they've been in current relationship",
  "Romantic love: total score of a 15-item scale measruing overall romantic love 1–5: Not at all to Extremely; no reverse coding; at least one valid response required, max score 75"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid gender category, and a continious variable between 0 and 100. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship duration  and
valid overall romantic love.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("PSY221A_Negrette/data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"PSY221A_Negrette/data/processed_data/h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"PSY221A_Negrette/data/processed_data/h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("PSY221A_Negrette/data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("PSY221A_Negrette/data/processed_data/h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
